messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing recurring 99p latency SLO misses on eu-west-1 this morning. 99p jumped from ~220ms -> 1.1s around 04:12 UTC and has stayed elevated.
ben: What does the batching telemetry say? max_batch pressure / admission queues?
maya: admission metrics look saturated. max_batch occupancy ~95-100% on several GPU shards. admission.queue_len spiking to 120-300 on hot shards. I suspect continuous stream of tiny prefill requests preventing good packing.
alex: Can you paste the last minute of batch_size distribution?
maya: Sure — grabbed from the trace logs:
```
batch_size.p50 = 3
batch_size.p90 = 7
batch_size.p99 = 14
max_batch = 16
continuous_maxbatch_occupancy = 97%
prefill_ratio = 0.62
```
maya: So a lot of small batches right up against max_batch but not filling it because many requests are 1-3 tokens prefill-heavy.
emily: If we lower max_batch we risk throughput; if we raise it we might OOM on certain kernels. Any memory headroom on those shards?
ben: Memory headroom is tight on the older A100 pool in eu-west-1. free_mem ~= 6GB on average, some shards dip to 1.2GB under heavy KV cache.
ops-bot: alert: eu-west-1: inference.slo.99p > 800ms for 14m — triggered at 04:12 UTC
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-2319 (eu-west-1 batch pressure)
alex: Two quick mitigations to try as a canary:
  1) Enable cross-request packer (enable_packer=true) for one allocation group to allow grouping of tiny prefills.
  2) Increase max_batch to 20 on one non-prod slice to measure latency/oom risk.
ben: +1 on canary. Add adaptive backoff for prefill-heavy traffic (prefer queuing > dropping) so we don't thrash admission.
maya: Running a quick canary: toggling feature flag on gpux-02 (non-prod slice) — PATCH via ops-api:
```
curl -XPOST $OPS_API/allocations/gpux-02/flags -d '{"enable_packer":true, "max_batch":20}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
alex: Also consider lowering pack_window_ms by 5-10ms to let packer combine tiny requests faster but beware tail latency jitter.
emily: Cost note — increasing max_batch/packer could increase GPU utilization by ~8-12% for this pool; need approval for temporary burst budget if we scale up.
ben: Observed another pattern: network variance on a single rack causing small delays that prevent co-arrival -> fragmentation. net_rx_jitter on node-7 is high. Might be a networking contrib.
maya: Good call — tracing shows node-7 shows repeated 1-5ms packet spikes during the incident window.
ops-bot: runbook reminder: when batch occupancy > 90% and 99p SLO breached -> try packer canary + single-slice max_batch bump, monitor for OOM and 95/99 latency.
alex: Results from gpux-02 canary after 6m:
```
max_batch_occupancy decreased 97% -> 68%
99p latency dropped 1.1s -> 340ms
no OOM observed
```
maya: Canary looks promising. Next steps:
  - Roll canary to two more slices in eu-west-1 with a 5-minute ramp
  - Run targeted net diagnostics on node-7 rack and rotate if jitter persists
  - Finance: flag for temporary burst budget for the pool until we fix packing or provision extra GPUs
emily: Please also add a safety throttle: if mem_free < 2GB revert max_batch and disable packer on that slice automatically.
ben: I'll open a provisioning request for +4 GPUs in eu-west-1 reserved for 72h as a safety buffer.
maya: I'll update the incident page with canary logs and attach traces. If ramp looks good we'll roll and schedule a postmortem to decide on longer-term options (packing behavior, model quantization / kernel changes, or resizing pool).
sre-bot: INC-2026-2319 updated: canary success on gpux-02. Action items created: #A1 (ramp), #A2 (network diag), #A3 (budget), #A4 (safety throttle).
alex: Thanks team. Quick note for follow-up: add metric for "packing_fragmentation_ratio" to console so we can alert earlier (p99 batch_fill_percentile < 60% while occupancy > 80%).
maya: Agreed. I'll draft the dashboard panels and a short runbook snippet.
